correctness.rationale: Every h_j is positive because the combined beneficial subtraction is bounded by 2P. Multiplication of the model's conditional survival probabilities makes maximizing survival equivalent to minimizing the sum of h_j; the 0-to-T interaction and baselines are constant. With z=|t−T/2| the derivative for z>0 has the sign of sinh(βz)/sinh(αz)−(α/(qβ))exp((β−α)T/2). This ratio is strictly increasing since u coth(uz) increases with u>0 (differentiate and use sinh x cosh x>x). Its limiting value at zero and its outer endpoint value give q_c and q_e, respectively. At equality the derivative has strict sign on the open half interval, proving exactly the claimed minimizers; otherwise the unique interior root is a strict half-interval minimum and reflection gives both minima. The derivative of ln q_e is α/(exp(αT)−1)−β/(exp(βT)−1)>0, and q_e increases from (α/β)² to α/β, whereas q_c increases to infinity and always exceeds q_e. Inverting the expansion of the ratio in z², coefficient (β²−α²)/6 after normalizing by β/α, proves z²=3(T−T_c)/(α+β)+O((T−T_c)²). For the persistent interior branch z→∞ as T→∞; writing the ratio as exp((β−α)z)(1−exp(−2βz))/(1−exp(−2αz)) gives t=T/2−z→ln(qβ/α)/(β−α), including zero at q=α/β. The sample thresholds also follow algebraically (at α=1,β=3, q=1/5 the endpoint root obeys 1+e^−T+e^−2T=5/3). The supplied checker is a grid and identity check inspected as text, not run; it is not a proof of global minima or an empirical validation.
residual_risks: The model is phenomenological with idealized instantaneous ordered events, no minimum gap and assumed additive memories. Neither the law nor any real exposure schedule was empirically validated.

originality.rationale: A distinct indexed result states the identical signed two-exponential optimization and complete fixed-horizon phase diagram, including the split onset and a stronger minimum-separation version. In its notation set a=α, b=β, A=P, B=D, r=A/B=1/q. Its maximized G is exactly −F_T; its cutoffs r_0, r_1 are exactly 1/q_c and 1/q_e. At fixed q, r/r_0(T)=exp((β−α)(T−T_c)/2), so the expansion of the same root at r/r_0=1 gives the stated fixed-q onset, including the error order by analytic inversion in z². The horizon-order cases and the far-horizon limit are direct monotonicity and exponential-limit readings of the same two cutoff functions and root, not a different optimization theorem. Dates alone do not establish precedence; the decision is exact mathematical coverage of the claimed classification and routine implications, not a claim about who published first.
